newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC completes Vietnam LPG storage, port.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC completes Vietnam LPG storage, port.

text.p: Taiwan state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Wednesday it has completed a 1,000-tonne liquid petroleum gas storage (LPG) facility and a port in Vietnam.
The LPG storage and a 5,000-tonne capacity off-loading port are in the northern Vietnam city of Haiphong, a company statement said.
The storage and port were build by a Chinese Petroleum managed joint-venture, formed in 1994, with Taiwan's Chinfon Group, and Vietnam's local firms, company officials said.
Chinese Petroleum officials said the joint-venture has already captured 20 percent of northern Vietnam's LPG market.
The officials declined to reveal further details.
Chinese Petroleum is seeking to form another joint-venture with Vietnam's Petro Vietnam to build a refinery with an annual capacity of 6.5 million tonnes at Dung Quat.
But no agreement has been reached so far.
Analysts have said Petro Vietnam is looking for better offers and terms from Chinese Petroleum or other bidders.
